name: Earth: geography and geology

objects.label: Materials
objects.text: EA.O.A1 Materials

objects.label: Minerals
objects.text: EA.O.A1.1 Minerals. IMA definition: a mineral is an element or compound, normally crystalline, formed by geological processes (Nickel 1995). Its composition is definite but not necessarily fixed, allowing solid solution. Silicates dominate the crust. Identification is by habit, cleavage, hardness, optics, XRD and microprobe. Names follow IMA (W12).

objects.label: Igneous rocks
objects.text: EA.O.A1.2 Igneous rocks. Formed from melt. Texture records cooling rate. Bowen's reaction series is the idealised crystallisation order of a basaltic melt cooling slowly with equilibrium reaction. Few magmas complete it. Classification follows IUGS (W12).

objects.label: Sedimentary rocks
objects.text: EA.O.A1.3 Sedimentary rocks. Formed by deposition and lithification. Grain size, sorting and composition are the descriptors. A sedimentary structure (cross-bed, ripple, graded bed) is evidence of the depositing process. Sedimentology is the A1 process claim; the sequence is EA.O.A3.

objects.label: Metamorphic rocks
objects.text: EA.O.A1.4 Metamorphic rocks. Formed by solid-state change. A metamorphic facies (Eskola 1920) is a set of mineral assemblages formed over a stated range of pressure and temperature. Foliation records directed stress. The rock cycle is a path among A1.2–A1.4, not a clock.

objects.label: Crustal fluids and element distribution
objects.text: EA.O.A1.5 Crustal fluids and element distribution. Groundwater, brines, hydrothermal fluids and melts in the crust. Element distribution in Earth reservoirs (geochemistry as distribution) is owned here. Speciation and reaction in a natural matrix is CH (uses CH, environmental chemistry cell). Soil parent material is here; the soil body is EA.O.A4.4.

objects.label: Internal motion
objects.text: EA.O.A2 Internal motion

objects.label: Plate kinematics
objects.text: EA.O.A2.1 Plate kinematics. The lithosphere is divided into plates that move relative to one another. Boundaries are divergent, convergent or transform. Evidence: continental fit, rock and fossil correlation, seafloor magnetic anomalies, seismicity, and geodetic motion. Euler-pole description of plate motion holds for rigid plates on a sphere.

objects.label: Deformation
objects.text: EA.O.A2.2 Deformation. Stress and strain in rock. Brittle faulting dominates near the surface; ductile flow dominates at depth. A fold is geometry; a fault is a fracture with offset. Earthquake size: magnitude is a logarithmic measure. Moment magnitude Mw derives from seismic moment M₀ = μAD (rigidity, rupture area, mean slip). Radiated energy rises about 32 times per unit magnitude. Intensity is felt effect (USGS, cited in audit).

objects.label: Interior structure and fields
objects.text: EA.O.A2.3 Interior structure and fields. Seismology infers layering from travel times. S waves do not pass through the outer core, which is evidence it is liquid. The geodynamo (the field generated in the liquid outer core) is owned here as an Earth-state claim. The MHD equations used are PH. Geodesy as a claim — figure of the Earth, gravity field — is owned here.

objects.label: Isostasy and flexure
objects.text: EA.O.A2.4 Isostasy and flexure. The lithosphere is in buoyant equilibrium on the asthenosphere. Airy compensation uses crustal roots; Pratt compensation uses lateral density change. Many ranges are partly supported by flexure of an elastic plate. Glacial isostatic adjustment is the observable rebound after ice load.

objects.label: Magmatism
objects.text: EA.O.A2.5 Magmatism. Melt generation at ridges (decompression), subduction zones (flux melting) and hotspots. A hotspot track is evidence of plate motion over a source, interpreted, not seen. Volcanic eruption as a hazard event enters EA.O.A5.5.

objects.label: Deep time
objects.text: EA.O.A3 Deep time

objects.label: Relative order
objects.text: EA.O.A3.1 Relative order. Steno (1669) gave superposition, original horizontality and lateral continuity. Superposition holds for undisturbed, non-overturned layered sequences. Cross-cutting relations are credited to Steno and Hutton. The principle of inclusions is Lyell's. An unconformity is evidence of missing time.

objects.label: Correlation
objects.text: EA.O.A3.2 Correlation. Matching strata between places by fossils, lithology, magnetic polarity, stable isotopes or tephra. An index fossil is widespread, short-lived and distinctive. A polarity reversal is a time marker, not a cause.

objects.label: Numeric age
objects.text: EA.O.A3.3 Numeric age. The decay law N = N₀e^(−λt) is owned by PH (uses PH nuclear cell). The dating claim is owned here. It holds when the system closed at a stated time, with known initial daughter and no later gain or loss. Carbon-14 serves late-Quaternary organic matter, to about 50,000 years. U–Pb and other systems serve deep time. Luminescence, dendrochronology and varves are other numeric methods.

objects.label: Time-scale convention
objects.text: EA.O.A3.4 Time-scale convention. The ICS chart divides eon, era, period, epoch and age. Phanerozoic and Ediacaran boundaries are GSSPs (reference sections). Most Precambrian boundaries are GSSAs, numeric ages such as 2500 Ma for Archean–Proterozoic. Warrant W12.

objects.label: Record of life and climate
objects.text: EA.O.A3.5 Record of life and climate. Occurrence of organisms in strata is owned here; their biology is BI.O.A4.5. Mass extinctions are pattern claims about that record. Paleoclimate and paleoceanography as dated states, read from proxies, are owned here. Their mechanism cites EA.O.A4.3. The Anthropocene as a formal unit was rejected by the IUGS in March 2024 (stratigraphy.org/news/152).

objects.label: Surface and fluid envelopes
objects.text: EA.O.A4 Surface and fluid envelopes

objects.label: Landforms and process
objects.text: EA.O.A4.1 Landforms and process. Geomorphology: landforms as products of rock, climate and time. Processes are weathering, mass wasting, fluvial, glacial, aeolian and coastal. A graded river adjusts slope and channel to its water and sediment load. The adjustment is a tendency, not a guarantee. Uniformitarianism is a methodological premise in EA.M.H, cited here.

objects.label: Water on and under land
objects.text: EA.O.A4.2 Water on and under land. Water balance for a drainage basin over a period: P = ET + Q + ΔS (precipitation, evapotranspiration, runoff, storage change). Groundwater and aquifer claims (transmissivity, storativity) are owned here. Darcy's law q = −K∇h holds for laminar flow (Reynolds number below about 1–10) in a saturated, rigid porous medium. Its owner is EN transport closure (uses EN.O.A2); CONTESTED, alternative PH continuum. The well is EN.

objects.label: Atmosphere, ocean and climate
objects.text: EA.O.A4.3 Atmosphere, ocean and climate. Climate is the statistics of weather over a stated period, typically 30 years (WMO). Its state, circulation and change as a dated Earth claim are owned here. Controls are latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents and circulation. The governing laws (Navier–Stokes, radiative transfer, thermodynamics) are PH. Ocean circulation, sea level and marine biogeochemical state are owned here; marine biology is BI.O.A5. Köppen–Geiger is a classification (W12), not a mechanism. Climate change attribution claims owe W2 and W5. Atmospheric electricity and the upper atmosphere are refused to PH (space physics).

objects.label: Cryosphere
objects.text: EA.O.A4.4 Cryosphere. Glaciers, ice sheets, sea ice, permafrost and snow as surface mass. Mass balance (accumulation minus ablation) is the core claim. Glacier flow by Glen's flow law assumes power-law creep of polycrystalline ice with exponent near 3 (UNVERIFIED exponent range). Glacial landforms are EA.O.A4.1.

objects.label: Soil
objects.text: EA.O.A4.5 Soil. The soil body: weathered parent material plus organic matter, organised in horizons. Pedology owns the profile here. Soil mechanics (effective stress, Mohr–Coulomb) is EN. Soil chemistry is CH. Soil biota are BI.O.A5.3.

objects.label: Human spatial organization
objects.text: EA.O.A5 Human spatial organization

objects.label: Location and interaction
objects.text: EA.O.A5.1 Location and interaction. Site and situation; absolute and relative location. Distance decay is the claim that interaction falls with distance, modified by origin and destination size. It is owned here. Gravity-model estimation is EA.M.5. In trade, the gravity equation has structural derivations (Anderson 1979; Anderson and van Wincoop 2003); that derivation is EC. In migration, gravity models are mostly reduced-form. CONTESTED for migration.

objects.label: Region and place
objects.text: EA.O.A5.2 Region and place. A region is a delimited area of stated similarity (formal), flow (functional) or perception (perceptual). Place is a location invested with meaning; its warrant is W8. Area studies as a catalog of regions is refused (sector, not a cell).

objects.label: Economic and urban pattern
objects.text: EA.O.A5.3 Economic and urban pattern. Where production and exchange happen. Central place theory predicts a hexagonal hierarchy on an isotropic plain with uniform population and transport, and rational, nearest-centre consumers. The spatial pattern is owned here. Bid-rent as allocation is EC. Urban models (concentric, sector, multiple nuclei) are ideal types.

objects.label: Political space
objects.text: EA.O.A5.4 Political space. Territory and boundary as spatial claims. A boundary is a claim enforced, not a natural line. The authority behind it is PO. Its legal validity is LA.

objects.label: Nature–society and risk
objects.text: EA.O.A5.5 Nature–society and risk. Coupled human–natural systems: pressure, state, impact and response, under a stated boundary. This absorbs environmental science claims (Grok "EV"). Risk = hazard × exposure × vulnerability (IPCC AR6 WGII glossary). Vulnerability is the propensity to be adversely affected: sensitivity plus lack of capacity to cope and adapt. Exposure is a separate factor. The hazard cites EA.O.A2 or A4. Policy is PO; price is EC; duty is LA. Population counts are MS.O.A5.

warrants.standard: Analytical identification (XRD, microprobe) with stated precision

warrants.defeaters: Solid solution misread as new species

warrants.warrant: W4, W2 (inversions with error), W6 (boundary comparison)
warrants.standard: Geodetic rates with uncertainty; tomography with resolution test
warrants.defeaters: Non-unique inversion; model dependence; sparse coverage

warrants.standard: Stratigraphic context; correlation by two independent methods
Stated decay constant, closure assumption and uncertainty
Field or remote measurement with accuracy assessment; process model calibrated and validated
Homogenised records with uncertainty; model ensembles with stated spread; detection and attribution
warrants.defeaters: Inhomogeneous records; model structural error; internal variability

warrants.standard: Place meaning traced to interview and text

sections.governing_thought: Earth science (geography and geology) is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Every Earth claim is about one of five questions: Materials · Internal motion · Deep time · Surface and fluid envelopes · Human spatial organization.
sections.key_line:
- Logic: inductive.
- Plural noun: questions about the Earth.
- Dimension: what the claim is about.
- Order: structural, from rock to settlement.

Members (5):
1. Materials
2. Internal motion
3. Deep time
4. Surface and fluid envelopes
5. Human spatial organization

Change from v1. "Surface pattern" becomes "Surface and fluid envelopes". This closes the ownership gap for ocean, atmosphere and cryosphere (audit error 11) without a sixth member. The laws used (fluid dynamics, radiative transfer, thermodynamics) remain PH. The dated Earth state and its circulation are EA. CONTESTED: alternative is a PH cell for climate mechanism with EA citing.

Dimension fix. v1 said "what the claim quantifies". Place meaning is not a quantity. The dimension is "what the claim is about" (audit error 5).
sections.assignment_rules:
1. A landform process is one claim, filed at EA.O.A4.1. The rock record of it is EA.O.A3. The equation is not filed twice.
2. GIS and cartography are methods (EA.M.4). GIScience is a bridge (EA.B.C8), not a claim about the Earth.
3. A fossil's biology is BI.O.A4.5. Its occurrence in a stratum is EA.O.A3.5.
4. Physical laws of fluids and radiation are PH. The dated state and circulation of ocean, atmosphere and ice are EA.O.A4.3–A4.4.
5. Decay law N = N₀e^(−λt) is PH. The age it gives under closure is EA.O.A3.3. Pharmacokinetic and first-order chemical half-lives are MD and CH; the registry disambiguates.
6. Groundwater flow claims are EA.O.A4.2. Darcy's law as closure is EN.O.A2 (contested). The well is EN.
7. Element distribution in Earth reservoirs is EA.O.A1.5. Speciation in a natural matrix is CH. Each cites the other.
8. Soil body and horizons are EA.O.A4.5. Effective stress and Mohr–Coulomb are EN.
9. Distance decay is EA.O.A5.1. Gravity-model estimation is EA.M.5. The trade gravity derivation is EC.
10. Bid-rent as allocation is EC. Its spatial pattern is EA.O.A5.3.
11. Boundary as spatial claim is EA.O.A5.4. Authority is PO. Validity is LA.
12. Risk = hazard × exposure × vulnerability is EA.O.A5.5. The hazard cites A2 or A4.
13. Environmental pressure–state–impact claims are EA.O.A5.5. Policy is PO; price is EC; duty is LA ("incidence is economics, the duty is law").
14. Biogeography is BI.O.A5.5 (contested). Biological C and N fluxes are BI.O.A5.4 (contested). EA cites both.
15. Human demography is MS.O.A5. Population geography cites it.
16. Seismic wave equation and elasticity are PH. Earth-structure inference is EA.O.A2.3.
17. Uniformitarianism is a heuristic (EA.M.H). It is never a cell.
18. A map projection theorem is MA. Its choice is EA.M.4.
19. Each sentence has one home. Others cite "uses EA.O.Ax.y".
